title: Year 12 Biology Module 6 – Genetic Change
description: A fast-recall review of NSW Year 12 Biology Module 6, organised by its three Inquiry Questions. Questions use short answers and avoid multi-step calculations or extended writing.
author: Generated with Classroom Jeopardy Quiz Maker

categories.name: How does mutation introduce new alleles?

questions.prompt: What is a change in the DNA sequence called?
What agent increases the rate of mutation?
What type of mutation changes a single nucleotide or base pair?
What type of mutation changes the structure or number of chromosomes?
What mutation occurs in a body cell and is generally not inherited by offspring?
What mutation occurs in cells that produce gametes and can be inherited?
questions.answer: A germ-line mutation. Accept: germline mutation.

questions.prompt: What process changes allele frequencies by random chance, especially in small populations?
What movement of alleles between populations occurs when individuals migrate and reproduce?

categories.name: How do genetic techniques affect biodiversity?

questions.prompt: What term describes the variety of living organisms, genes and ecosystems?
What term describes the use of biological systems or organisms to develop useful products or processes?
What type of biodiversity refers to variation in genes and alleles within a species?
What term describes an organism whose genetic material has been deliberately altered using biotechnology?
questions.answer: A genetically modified organism. Accept: GMO.

questions.prompt: What modern gene-editing system uses a guide RNA and a Cas enzyme?
What agricultural system growing one genetically similar crop over a large area can reduce genetic diversity?
What facility stores seeds to preserve plant genetic diversity for future use?
What field considers the ethical issues raised by biological and genetic technologies?

categories.name: Can DNA manipulation change populations forever?

questions.prompt: What reproductive technology places sperm into the female reproductive tract without natural mating?
What plant reproductive technology deliberately transfers pollen between selected plants?
What process produces a genetically identical copy of a whole organism?
What process makes many copies of a particular gene or DNA sequence?
What small circular DNA molecule is commonly used as a vector in bacteria?
What enzymes cut DNA at specific recognition sequences?
What technology combines DNA from different sources into one DNA molecule?
What term describes an organism containing a gene introduced from another organism?

finalRound.prompt: What process is the ultimate source of new alleles in a population?
